evidence: paper: |\partial_z^a \partial_t^b q| \le C_{a,b}\, q^{\,1-aD-b}, \qquad a, b \ge 0, \qquad 0 < D < 1.

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. Lean has no D-discount in the q-jet bound it assumes or proves: everywhere the loss is one power of q per derivative, i.e. the exponent 1 - m for the full space-time jet of order m, which is the D = 1 case of (5.28) — a value the paper's range 0 < D < 1 excludes. Direction of the implication: for 0 < q ≤ 1 one has q^{1-aD-b} ≤ q^{1-a-b}, so (5.28) with any 0 < D < 1 implies the Lean hypothesis (q is independent of the transverse variables, which Lean enforces through CutStageEstimates.physicalProjection, so only z and t derivatives occur); hence the Lean summation lemma consumes a weaker hypothesis than the paper's, and the actual similarity coordinate is proved to satisfy it (physicalQ_jet_bound). Conversely the Lean statement does not give the paper's sharper bound for a ≥ 2; the only D-weighted statement I found is the exact first-order rate ∂_z q = 2η q^{1-D}/L (qAxial_rpow), with the time rate -1/L. Rated low rather than none because the paper's inequality as written is not the one checked, even though what Lean checks suffices for the Lean development.
